# Upgrading @artisanpack-ui/react 1.x to 2.0

<!-- Generated by packages/codemods/scripts/build-guides.mjs from packages/codemods/guides/react.md and the upgrade rules. Do not edit; run `npm run guides --workspace @artisanpack-ui/codemods`. -->

`@artisanpack-ui/react` 2.0 is rebuilt on the ArtisanPack UI design system. The components keep their purpose, and three things change underneath them:

- **DaisyUI is gone.** Components are styled by `@artisanpack-ui/css`: plain CSS in cascade layers, driven by design tokens. Tailwind is optional.
- **One API across Livewire, React and Vue.** Some components, props and events were renamed to match. Most 1.x exports still work in 2.0, marked `@deprecated`, so an app keeps building while you migrate, but they go in the next major.
- **Theming is tokens.** `@artisanpack-ui/tokens` 2.0 replaces the DaisyUI color maps with presets built on the tokens.

The codemod does the mechanical part. This guide covers it and what is left for you.

## How long the old version is supported

The previous major gets **security fixes only for 12 months** after the new one ships. No features or component fixes are backported. Each repository's `SECURITY.md` carries the end date from launch day.

The old and new majors can't be mixed in one app: the new CSS replaces DaisyUI, and the two style the same components differently. Upgrade a whole app at once, on a branch.

## 1. Update the packages

Commit your work first, then:

```bash
npm install @artisanpack-ui/react@^2 @artisanpack-ui/css
npm uninstall daisyui
```

## 2. Run the codemod

Preview the changes:

```bash
npx @artisanpack-ui/codemods react src --dry-run
```

The dry run prints a diff of every file it would change and writes nothing. Run it without `--dry-run` to apply them:

```bash
npx @artisanpack-ui/codemods react src
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| paths | Files or directories to migrate. Default: `src` |
| `--dry-run` | Show the changes as a diff without writing |
| `--no-classes` | Leave raw DaisyUI classes out of the report |
| `--json` | Print the report as JSON |

It reads `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.ts` and `.js` files and skips `node_modules`, build output and dot-directories. It edits in place and keeps your formatting and comments; run your formatter afterwards if a rewritten line runs long.

**What it rewrites.** Imports from `@artisanpack-ui/react` and its entry points (`/form`, `/layout`, …), with every reference to a renamed component and its `Props` type; renamed props and events on JSX elements; flags that became values (`vertical` to `orientation="vertical"`); values that changed with the name (`position="left"` to `placement="start"`); and per-part class props, merged into `classes`. It follows aliases (`Modal as Sheet`) and namespace imports (`UI.Modal`).

**What it reports and leaves alone.** Each line of the report has the file, line and column:

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `manual` | A prop, event or component with no automatic replacement. The message says what to do |
| `review` | A change that was made and deserves a look: a renamed event whose payload changed, or a dynamic value the codemod couldn't read |
| `removed` | A prop that was deleted because 2.0 has no equivalent |
| `class` | A raw DaisyUI class, theme variable or DaisyUI configuration. See step 3 |

It can't see through a spread (`<Modal {...props} />`) or a dynamic value (`vertical={isTall}`); both are reported. You can run the codemod again after you fix things by hand: migrated code has nothing left for it to rewrite. The exception is a 1.x name that 2.0 reuses with a new meaning, such as `label` on Code. Preview a second run with `--dry-run`.

## 3. Remove DaisyUI and adopt the new CSS

Load the CSS once. Without Tailwind, import it in your app's entry:

```ts
import '@artisanpack-ui/css';
```

With Tailwind v4, import it from your Tailwind entry stylesheet instead. Declare the layer order first, so Preflight never restyles a component and a utility on a component still wins. The last import is optional: it adds utilities generated from the tokens (`bg-surface-page`, `text-muted`, `rounded-control`).

```css
@layer theme, base, apui, components, utilities;
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@artisanpack-ui/css';
@import '@artisanpack-ui/css/tailwind';
```

Then delete `@plugin "daisyui";` and any `@plugin "daisyui/theme"` block from your CSS.

To bring your own styles, import `@artisanpack-ui/css/headless` instead: the same markup, ARIA and behavior with no component CSS.

### Replace raw DaisyUI classes

Markup that used DaisyUI classes directly (`btn`, `card`, `badge`, `bg-base-200`) has no styles once DaisyUI is gone. The upgrade tool lists every one with its file and line and **never rewrites them**, because the right replacement depends on the element. For each:

| You have | Use instead |
|---|---|
| A component class: `btn`, `badge`, `card`, `alert`, `tab`, `modal`, `tooltip`, … | The component. `<a class="btn btn-primary">` is a Button with `href`. Where you need the bare markup, the `apui-` class and data attributes: `class="apui-button" data-color="primary"` |
| A size or color modifier: `btn-sm`, `badge-success`, `alert-warning` | The component's `size` and `color` props (`data-size`, `data-color` on bare markup) |
| `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `checkbox`, `toggle`, `label` on native controls | The form components, which draw the label, hint and error too |
| `bg-base-100` | `bg-surface-default` with the Tailwind preset, or `background: var(--apui-surface-default)` |
| `bg-base-200` | `bg-surface-sunken` · `var(--apui-surface-sunken)` |
| `bg-base-300`, `border-base-300` | `border-default` · `var(--apui-border-default)`; as a background, `bg-surface-sunken` |
| `text-base-content` | `text-default` · `var(--apui-text-default)` |
| `text-base-content/70`, `/60`, `/50` | `text-muted` · `var(--apui-text-muted)`. `text-subtle` for the faintest text. Opacity on text is gone: the tokens are checked for contrast, an opacity isn't |
| `text-primary-content`, `text-error-content`, … | The color's own foreground: `text-primary-foreground`, `text-error-foreground` · `var(--apui-color-primary-foreground)`, `var(--apui-color-error-foreground)` |
| `bg-primary`, `text-error`, `border-success` | Unchanged with the Tailwind preset. Without Tailwind, the color's own token: `var(--apui-color-primary)`, `var(--apui-color-error)`, `var(--apui-color-success)` |
| `rounded-box`, `rounded-btn` | `rounded-surface`, `rounded-control` · `var(--apui-radius-surface)`, `var(--apui-radius-control)` |

The tool marks names such as `input`, `table`, `link` and `label` as "may be": they are DaisyUI classes and also common class names of your own. Check each.

Left and right are logical now. Use `ms-*`, `me-*`, `ps-*`, `pe-*`, `start-*` and `end-*` next to components so layouts mirror in right-to-left languages.

## 4. Migrate your theme

`@artisanpack-ui/tokens` 1.x shipped DaisyUI color maps, `cn()`, `resolveColor()`, glass helpers and a Tailwind plugin. 2.0 replaces all of them with the design tokens as `--apui-*` custom properties, which `@artisanpack-ui/css` already includes. Remove the 1.x Tailwind plugin from your config and any imports of those helpers.

A brand is a **preset**. The generator ships with the tokens package, so install it, then generate a preset from your colors:

```bash
npm install --save-dev @artisanpack-ui/tokens@^2
npx apui-generate-preset --name acme --primary "#7c3aed" > acme.css
```

The generator refuses a preset that fails WCAG 2.2 AA contrast in any theme. Import the file after `@artisanpack-ui/css` and switch it on with `<html data-preset="acme">`.

The theme lives in `data-theme` on `<html>`. ThemeToggle sets and stores it and reports a change as `onValueChange`; its `modes` prop is now `choices`. Render `ThemeScript` in the document head to apply the stored theme before first paint.

### Repoint theme variables

DaisyUI's custom properties are gone, and nothing aliases them. The tool lists each reference:

| DaisyUI | Token |
|---|---|
| `--color-base-100` | `--apui-surface-default` |
| `--color-base-200` | `--apui-surface-sunken` |
| `--color-base-300` | `--apui-border-default` |
| `--color-base-content` | `--apui-text-default` |
| `--color-primary`, `--color-error`, … | `--apui-color-primary`, `--apui-color-error`, … |
| `--color-primary-content` | `--apui-color-primary-foreground` |
| `--radius-box` | `--apui-radius-surface` |
| `--radius-field` | `--apui-radius-field` |
| `--radius-selector` | `--apui-radius-control` |
| `var(--p)`, `var(--b1)`, `var(--bc)` (DaisyUI 4) | The same tokens as above |

`--color-*` is also a Tailwind theme namespace, so some of these may be yours and not DaisyUI's. The tool can't tell; you can.

### Themes and presets

| Before | Now |
|---|---|
| `data-theme="light"` or a DaisyUI theme name | `data-theme="light"`, `"dark"` or `"high-contrast"`. With no attribute the page follows the system setting |
| A custom DaisyUI theme, or a generated theme file | A **preset**: a named set of token values switched with `data-preset`. `ledger` and `harbor` ship with the CSS |
| Glass props with tints and opacities | `surface="glass"` on the component; the look comes from the glass tokens |
| Per-component color overrides | Tokens. Set `--apui-color-primary` and the rest once, in a preset |

Theme, preset and density (`data-density="compact"`) combine, and any element can set them for its subtree.

## 5. Renamed and consolidated components

| 1.x | Now | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `<Dropdown>` | `<DropdownMenu>` |  |
| `<DropdownItem>` | By hand | Use `DropdownMenuItem`, which needs a `value`; the menu reports the choice through `onSelect`. |
| `<Editor>` | `<CodeEditor>` |  |
| `<ErrorDisplay>` | `<ErrorState>` |  |
| `<Modal>` | `<Dialog>` |  |
| `<Radio>` | `<RadioGroup>` |  |
| `<Sidebar>` | By hand | Use `AppShell`, the whole page frame, with a `Menu` in its `sidebar` slot. |
| `<SpotlightSearch>` | `<Spotlight>` |  |
| `<StatGroup>` | `<Grid>` |  |
| `<ToastMessage>` | By hand | Use `Toast`, which takes `title`, `description` and `color` instead of a `toast` object. |
| `<ToastProvider>` | By hand | Render one `<Toaster />` instead of wrapping the app, and create toasts with `toast.create()`. |

## 6. Changes by component

Every 1.x prop and event that changed. "Automatic" says whether the codemod makes the change for you.

### `<Accordion>`

| 1.x | 2.0 | Automatic |
|---|---|---|
| `openIndices` | Now `value`. | Yes |
| `defaultOpenIndices` | Now `defaultValue`. | Yes |
| `join` | Remove `join`. If it was `join={false}` (separate panels), use `variant="separated"`. | By hand |
| `onOpenChange` | The `onOpenChange` event is not in the 2.0 API. Check the component's docs for what replaces it. | By hand |

### `<Alert>`

| 1.x | 2.0 | Automatic |
|---|---|---|
| `visible` | Removed. Alert dismisses itself; listen to `open-change`. | Yes |
| `onDismiss` | Now `onOpenChange`. Check the handler: the payload is boolean. | Yes, to review |

| `online` | Now `status="online"`. | Yes |
| `offline` | Now `status="offline"`. | Yes |
| `subtitle` | Avatar no longer renders a title or subtitle. Render the text beside it, for example in a `ListItem` (`title`, `description`, `leading`). | By hand |

| `strokeWidth` | Remove it: the stroke width is set by the design system. | By hand |
| `curve` | Removed. Lines are drawn by the shared geometry; there is no curve switch. | Yes |
| `fillOpacity` | Remove it: use `variant="area"` for a fill; its opacity is set by the design system. | By hand |
| `showTooltip` | Removed. Sparkline has no hover tooltip; it is described by `label`. | Yes |

### `<SpotlightSearch>` → `<Spotlight>`

| 1.x | 2.0 | Automatic |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | Use `groups`: wrap the items as `[{ label, items }]` and rename item fields to the `SpotlightResult` shape (`label`, `description`, `href`, `icon`, `keywords`). | By hand |
| `filterFn` | No custom filter. Set `remote`, track the query with `search`/`onSearchChange`, and pass already-filtered `groups`. | By hand |
| `maxResults` | Remove it: there is no result cap. Limit the items you pass (with `remote` if you filter yourself). | By hand |
| `emptyMessage` | Now `emptyLabel`. | Yes |
| `onClose` | Now `onOpenChange`. Check the handler: the payload is boolean. | Yes, to review |

## 7. After the codemod

- Work through the `manual` lines of the report, then the `class` lines.
- **Events.** Value and open changes are `onValueChange` and `onOpenChange`. The codemod renames handlers and marks each for review, because the payload is now the value and not a DOM event.
- **Toasts.** `ToastProvider` no longer wraps the app. Render one `Toaster` and create toasts with `toast.create()`.
- **Left and right.** Placement and side props take `start` and `end`, so layouts mirror in right-to-left languages.
- Run the type checker: every prop the codemod left behind is a type error that points at the line.
- Look at each page in light, dark and high-contrast themes.
